items.title: What does a concession trade actually do to deal value?
items.description: This models Dana and Marcus's final trade from L3: Dana gives up a discount off the $24,000/year list price, in exchange for a longer locked contract term. A discount alone always reduces the deal's annual value — but each extra year locked in also protects that price against future increases (assumed at 6%/year if the deal were re-negotiated yearly instead), which raises the trade's effective value over the full contract. At the default of a 17.5% discount and a 2-year term (Dana and Marcus's actual numbers), the effective annual value lands close to what Dana actually walked away with. Drag the discount higher to see how much term length has to grow to still make the trade worth it — and notice a 1-year term never recovers a large discount, since there's no extra time locked in for the protection to apply over.

params.name: discountPercent
params.label: Discount given off the $24,000/year list price

params.name: termYears
params.label: Contract term locked in, in exchange

items.compute: const list = 24000; const discounted = list * (1 - params.discountPercent / 100); const annualIncrease = 0.06; let protectedValue = 0; for (let y = 0; y < params.termYears; y++) { protectedValue += list * Math.pow(1 + annualIncrease, y); } const oneYearBaseline = list * params.termYears; const effectiveAnnualValue = discounted + (protectedValue - oneYearBaseline) / params.termYears; return { effectiveAnnualValue: Math.round(effectiveAnnualValue) };

outputs.label: Effective annual value of the trade
